newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Discount Bank to delay offer until April.
newsitem.headline: Discount Bank to delay offer until April.

text.p: Israel Discount Bank said on Sunday it would delay a secondary offering of shares and warrants scheduled for this month until April.

"Discount Bank requests to announce that it still does not have the figures on financial costs for the fourth quarter of 1996 at the required level of certainty and cannot meet the requirements for publication of a prospectus based on its financial reports of the first nine months of 1996," the bank said in an announcement ot the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

The bank said it expects to approve its audited financial reports for full-year 1996 only on March 24, 1997 and that it would present a new prospectus for approval by the Securities Authority in early April.

Discount, Israel's third-largest commercial bank, was due to make an offering of 17 percent of equity now held by the Israeli government during February. The offering was to be for a minimum of 600 million shekels.

However, the bank said on February 14 the Securities Authority refused to approve the prospectus after Discount said it expected a big increase in its fourth-quarter doubtful-debt provision. The increase, it added, would reduce earnings.

Since then the bank, together with MI Holdings, the government company charged with selling the state's bank shares, had been seeking to provide more exact data. The bank had until February 28 to meet Securities Authority requirements before the deadline for issuing shares based on nine-month results expired.
A Discount spokeswoman said the bank intended to keep to the dates cited in today's announcements for the offering.
"This is the earliest possible date, that is what we want to do," she said.

An institutional pre-offering, which had been completed successfully prior to the problems with Securities Authority, would be cancelled since the new offering would be based on Discount's full-year results, the spokeswoman added.
Discount, one of several banks taken over by the government in the wake of the 1983 bank shares crash, is 79 percent controlled by the State of Israel.
